finding: Not-listed worktree folder fallback re-implemented in h2_move.target, and it drops the creator's folder check
why: The chain AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER, then the provider JSON key, then .claude/worktrees has two homes (create-worktree:276-277 and here). h2_move's copy lacks the refusal at create-worktree:399 for an absolute or '..' folder, so the planned path can differ from where --name actually goes (the creator refuses).

finding: record() relies on os.link with no fallback; a filesystem without hard links stops every move
why: The old `open(marker, 'x')` worked on any filesystem. `os.link` raises OSError (not FileExistsError) on a .git folder on FAT/exFAT or a share or mount without hard links, so plan() raises on every call. The sibling afk-move.py:132-134 already falls back when `os.replace` fails; this site does not.
fix: On an OSError that is not FileExistsError, fall back to `open(marker, 'x')` and `json.dump`. A torn read is now handled by the ValueError branch.
evidence: h2_move.py:104-110 catches only FileExistsError. A session whose `<common>/afk-session` sits on a link-less volume: `os.link(whole, marker)` raises OSError(EPERM/ENOTSUP), it propagates from plan(), and protected_branch_guard.py:453 turns it into '(the worktree could not be started: ...)' on every refused call. No move is ever recorded.

finding: record(): a failed cleanup of the temp name turns a recorded move into an exception, so no creation starts
why: `finally: whole.unlink(missing_ok=True)` runs after `os.link` has already made the marker. On Windows the unlink raises PermissionError while a scanner or another process holds the new temp file. The exception replaces `return True`, plan() raises, and h2_hint reports 'could not be started'. The marker now exists and is fresh, so every later call returns `chosen` without spawning, and nothing starts until RETRY_AFTER (180 s) passes.
fix: Wrap the cleanup unlink in `try/except OSError: pass`, since the marker is already recorded, or unlink outside the try/finally after the return value is decided.
evidence: h2_move.py:104-110 `try: os.link(whole, marker); return True ... finally: whole.unlink(missing_ok=True)`. `missing_ok` only covers FileNotFoundError. Failing sequence: the first refused call writes `whole`, `os.link` succeeds, the unlink raises PermissionError. plan() at :129 never reaches the spawn at :146. The next call finds the marker (:125) and returns at :141 because `time.time() - marker.stat().st_mtime < RETRY_AFTER`. Reached by reading; not run.

finding: plan() deletes an in-flight move's marker when it reads a torn write, and the helper's non-atomic fallback can produce one
why: The ValueError branch assumes 'markers are written whole'. afk-move.py:132-134 breaks that: on Windows `os.replace` fails with PermissionError while plan() has the marker open for reading (Python opens without share-delete), and the fallback `target.write_text` truncates in place. A reader that catches the empty or partial file unlinks the live marker and re-plans.
fix: Before unlinking, re-read once after a short sleep and treat the marker as corrupt only if it is still unparseable. Also make the helper's fallback atomic, or skip the in-place rewrite and leave the marker as is.
evidence: h2_move.py:135-137 `except ValueError: marker.unlink(missing_ok=True) ... return plan(...)`. afk-move.py:130-134 `try: os.replace(whole, target) except OSError: ... target.write_text(json.dumps(body))`. Interleaving: helper A is finishing, hook call B is in `read_text`, A's replace fails, A truncates and rewrites, B parses an empty or partial string and raises ValueError, B unlinks A's marker and replans. A second `session-<hex>` creation starts, and A's later outcome is no longer in the session's marker. Reached by reading; not run.

finding: Parent-mode heredoc re-derives path containment that placement.py owns, and uses bare string literals for states and rules
why: The inside-main prefix test (realpath, normcase, startswith) repeats placement._below. The bash block at 368-377 and check_target (placement.py:246-247) both expand '~' and absolutize. The literals "refused" and "main" stand in for placement.REFUSED and OUTSIDE. "main" is not a catalog rule id but is carried in the P_RULE field next to real R-nn ids.
fix: Move the main-checkout containment check into placement.py, which returns a named Verdict, and have the heredoc relay it without its own path logic.
evidence: line 306 `inside_main = os.path.normcase(target).startswith(os.path.normcase(main.rstrip("\\/") + os.sep))`; line 308 `return "refused", target, main, "main", ""`; line 333 `"$P_RULE" == outside || "$P_RULE" == main`

finding: record() swaps the old exclusive open for os.link with no fallback, so a filesystem without hard links fails every move plan
why: Only FileExistsError is caught; any other OSError from os.link (a volume or share without hard links) escapes plan(), which worked there before, and a write_text failure before the try leaves its temp file behind. Narrow reach (inferred, not run): the guard's h2_hint catches the exception and degrades to a fallback hint.
fix: On a non-FileExistsError OSError fall back to open(marker, 'x'), as afk-move.record falls back when os.replace fails; move the temp write inside the try so the finally removes it.
evidence: h2_move.py:104-110 `try: os.link(whole, marker); return True / except FileExistsError: return False / finally: whole.unlink(missing_ok=True)` against the replaced `with open(marker, "x", encoding="utf-8")`; contrast scripts/afk-move.py:130-134 `except OSError: ... target.write_text(...)`

finding: A transient read failure of an existing marker is reported as 'session worktree could not be created'
why: `marker.exists()` at :125 is True, but another call's `unlink` (:139) or remove-worktree's drop_markers can delete it before `read_text`. The resulting FileNotFoundError (also a Windows sharing PermissionError during the helper's replace) goes to the OSError branch, which returns an `error`, not a re-plan. The hook then tells the agent the creation failed when nothing failed.
fix: Treat FileNotFoundError as 'no marker' and re-plan. For other OSErrors, retry the read once before returning the error. The same race can raise from `marker.stat()` at :141.
evidence: h2_move.py:131-134 `except OSError as problem: return {..., 'error': f'move record: {problem}'}`; protected_branch_guard.py:455-458 renders any `error` as 'the session worktree could not be created: ...'. The old code returned a path in this case. test_h2_move.py covers only a directory in the marker's place, not a vanished file.

finding: A torn read now unlinks the live marker, but afk-move.record still has a non-atomic write path
why: The unlink assumes markers are always written whole, yet afk-move.py:133-134 falls back to target.write_text when os.replace fails (a Windows reader holding the file open). A plan() call reading that torn write deletes the marker and starts a second creation, and the helper's outcome write then finds no marker (read raises OSError, swallowed). Reached by reading; not run.
fix: Do not unlink on ValueError. Retry the read briefly, then report an error. Or drop the non-atomic fallback in afk-move.record and let a failed replace leave the marker unchanged.
evidence: h2_move.py:136 `marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)  # markers are written whole, so this one is corrupt`; afk-move.py:131-134 `os.replace(whole, target) ... except OSError: whole.unlink(missing_ok=True); target.write_text(json.dumps(body), encoding="utf-8")`
